functions.name: account.members
functions.description: The users page of an organization: members with their sign-in details.

functions.name: account.permissions
functions.description: The caller's effective permissions in an organization, for the UI.

functions.name: account.updateLogo
functions.description: Sets an organization's logo to an uploaded image (same limits as an avatar), to an image URL, or to none, removing any previously uploaded file.

functions.name: applications.applications.getWebhookUrl
functions.description: The URL deploys the application without further auth, so it takes the permission to edit the application (its refreshToken).

functions.name: applications.applications.saveDockerSource
functions.description: The password is encrypted here; pass undefined to keep the stored one and "" to clear it.

functions.name: applications.applications.saveEnvironment
functions.description: Only the provided fields change; "" clears one.

functions.name: applications.applications.updateNetworks
functions.description: Sets the extra networks and whether the service leaves panara-cloud-network; applied on the next deploy.

functions.name: applications.deploy.cancelDeployments
functions.description: Stops only this application's builds, not every build on the host.

functions.name: applications.deploy.cleanQueues
functions.description: Drops deployments that have not started yet.

functions.name: applications.deploy.clearDeployments
functions.description: Deletes finished deployments and their logs, keeping queued/running ones and the latest successful deployment.

functions.name: applications.deploy.dropDeploy
functions.description: Deploys an uploaded zip: it was uploaded with generateDropUploadUrl; the agent downloads and unpacks it on the build server.

functions.name: applications.deploy.killBuild
functions.description: The agent kills the running build when its job is cancelled.

functions.name: applications.deploy.reload
functions.description: Re-applies the service spec (env, mounts, resources) with the current image.

functions.name: applications.deploy.webhookBaseUrl
functions.description: Base of the deploy webhook URLs (`<base>/<token>`, `<base>/compose/<token>`): they are served by the Convex site, not the web app.

functions.name: applications.patchRepo.requestTree
functions.description: Clones (or refreshes) the repository and lists its tracked files.

functions.name: applications.patchRepo.result
functions.description: The parsed result once the job finished: a file tree for "tree", the file content for "read".

functions.name: applications.patches.save
functions.description: Creates or updates a patch; one patch per file.

functions.name: applications.previews.redeploy
functions.description: Rebuilds the code already on the build server (rebuild: true, a preview redeploy) or clones the pull request branch again.

functions.name: applications.settings.overview
functions.description: Everything the application page shows: the application (without its webhook token) plus the names and addresses of its server, environment and project.

functions.name: applications.settings.updateServiceSettings
functions.description: Swarm and resource settings, one form at a time: the given fields are set and the ones in `clear` go back to Docker's defaults. Takes effect on the next deploy or reload.

functions.name: compose.containers.refresh
functions.description: Queues a fresh `containers` snapshot of the compose's host; repeated requests collapse into the one already waiting.

functions.name: compose.crud.one
functions.description: A compose service: the row plus the server, environment and project names its page shows.

functions.name: compose.deploy.clearDeployments
functions.description: Deletes finished deployments and their logs, keeping queued/running ones and the latest successful deployment.

functions.name: compose.deploy.convert
functions.description: Converted, randomized and isolated-deployment previews: the compose file as the next deploy would write it, or with the randomize / isolated deployment values of an unsaved form. A randomize preview without a suffix uses a random one.

functions.name: compose.deploy.killBuild
functions.description: Cancelling the running deploy job makes the agent kill the deploy script's whole process group (docker compose build/up and everything it spawned); see runScript in apps/agent/src/compose.

functions.name: compose.deploy.loadServices
functions.description: Lists the compose file's services ("fetch" clones the source again; "cache" reads what is on the host) and refreshes the source (fetch: true). The service names land on the compose row; failures on the op.

functions.name: compose.deploy.removeDeployment
functions.description: Removes one compose deployment.

functions.name: compose.hostOps.loadMounts
functions.description: The named volumes the service's running container uses, as Docker reports them (JSON array of mounts).

functions.name: compose.hostOps.requestPatchTree
functions.description: Clones (or refreshes) the repository and lists its tracked files.

functions.name: compose.mounts.list
functions.description: File mounts are written to /etc/panara-cloud/compose/<appName>/files/<filePath> and referenced from the compose file as ../files/<filePath>.

functions.name: compose.templates.deployTemplate
functions.description: Deploys a template: a catalog template becomes a new raw compose service with its generated env, domains and file mounts.

functions.name: compose.templates.importTemplate
functions.description: Imports a template: replaces an existing compose service's file, env, domains and file mounts with a base64 `{ compose, config }` template.

functions.name: compose.templates.processTemplate
functions.description: Previews a template import: what importing the template would write (variables resolved), for the preview before the import. Generated values change on every call.

functions.name: databases.backups.listFiles
functions.description: Lists this backup's files in its destination folder, newest first; the UI follows `api.databases.destinations.opResult({ opId })`.

functions.name: databases.backups.restore
functions.description: Restores a dump into a database (or a compose service, using the credentials of `backupId`). The file may come from any folder of the destination, so a backup can be restored into a fresh database.

functions.name: databases.backups.restoreCompose
functions.description: The compose restore form: the service and its database credentials are typed in (postgres: user; mariadb/mongo: user and password; mysql: root password). The password only lives until the restore ends.

functions.name: databases.backups.setCredentials
functions.description: Compose backups only: the password the dump runs with (mysql: root).

functions.name: databases.databases.connection
functions.description: Hosts, ports and connection URLs. Passwords are only included for admins: only privileged users see database credentials.

functions.name: databases.databases.one
functions.description: Everything a database's page shows: the row, its server, environment and project names, its mounts and, for admins, its passwords.

functions.name: databases.databases.rebuild
functions.description: Rebuild: deletes the data volumes and recreates the service. Not idempotent: a retry after a crash must not wipe data restored since.

functions.name: databases.databases.saveExternalPort
functions.description: Publishes (or unpublishes, with null) the database on the host and redeploys it.

functions.name: databases.databases.updateNetworks
functions.description: Sets the extra networks and whether the service leaves panara-cloud-network; applied on the next deploy.

functions.name: databases.databases.updateServiceSettings
functions.description: Replaces all swarm and resource settings at once, as the settings form submits them together. Takes effect on the next deploy.

functions.name: databases.destinations.listFiles
functions.description: Backups live under <appName>/ or, for compose services, under <appName>_<serviceName>/; members only browse the folders of services they were given. Browses the bucket's backup files: `search` is a path whose last segment filters names in that folder.

functions.name: databases.destinations.remove
functions.description: Removing a destination also deletes the backups that point at it.

functions.name: databases.destinations.testConnection
functions.description: Tests a saved destination, or unsaved form values (draft) before saving, by running `rclone ls` on the panel host or the given server. A draft that leaves the secret blank while editing (destinationId given) is tested with the destination's stored secret.

functions.name: databases.destinations.update
functions.description: Omit secretAccessKey to keep the stored one.

functions.name: databases.panelBackups.listFiles
functions.description: Lists the archives in this backup's folder, newest first; the UI follows `api.databases.destinations.opResult({ opId })`.

functions.name: databases.panelBackups.restore
functions.description: Restores /etc/panara-cloud from an archive and stages its Convex snapshot for a manual `convex import` (an import replaces the jobs table this job runs from, so it can't be part of the job).

functions.name: databases.volumeBackups.restore
functions.description: Restores a tar archive into a volume on the owner's host. It refuses when a container (running or stopped) still uses the volume.

functions.name: email.saveProvider
functions.description: The key is encrypted here (actions only: IVs need real randomness) and is never returned to the client; only its last four characters are kept in the clear so the page can tell keys apart.

functions.name: email.sendTest
functions.description: Sends synchronously so the page can show the provider's answer.

functions.name: environments.deletableVolumes
functions.description: For the delete dialog: per service, its appName and what deleting it with its volumes would do to each named volume as far as the panel's own definitions tell (`keptBecause` names the services outside `targets` that still use it). `volumes` is null for a compose service read from Git, whose volumes are declared on its server. Containers are looked at only when the removal runs: the job reports what it kept.

functions.name: environments.duplicate
functions.description: Duplicates an environment: a new environment with the same description and shared variables; services are not copied.

functions.name: environments.get
functions.description: The environment page header: the environment, its project and whether the caller may open it (null for unknown ids or other organizations, so a stale link renders "not found" instead of throwing).

functions.name: environments.services
functions.description: Services of one environment with what the service cards show: server name and the time of the latest deployment.

functions.name: infra.basicAuth.create
functions.description: Hashing runs in an action so the salt comes from a real CSPRNG.

functions.name: infra.certificates.get
functions.description: Returns the public chain; never the private key.

functions.name: infra.certificates.listDetailed
functions.description: The certificates screen: each certificate with its public chain (expiry and CN are parsed in the browser) and its server.

functions.name: infra.cleanup.cancelQueuedDeployments
functions.description: "Clean all deployment queue": cancels the organization's builds and deploys that are still waiting for a slot. Running jobs are untouched.

functions.name: infra.connect.status
functions.description: Connect status: the server registered by the command generated for this key, once it ran.

functions.name: infra.connectNode.generateCommand
functions.description: Generates the connect command: a new SSH key named after the server plus a single-use token valid for an hour. The UI turns the token into `curl -fsSL <panel>/api/connect/<token> | sudo bash`.

functions.name: infra.docker.cleanup
functions.description: Manual clean-ups, run once. They remove what is unused on the whole host, including what Panara Cloud did not create. "all" is what the nightly clean-up runs and skips volumes, which only the "volumes" scope removes.

functions.name: infra.docker.health
functions.description: Queues a health check of the host; read the result with snapshots.opResult.

functions.name: infra.docker.listAppContainers
functions.description: Container pickers of the logs and terminal dialogs: containers by app name match (service.read) and by app label ("swarm"/"standalone", docker.read). On the panel host everyone except its instance administrators only gets containers labelled with their organization. Read the result with snapshots.opResult.

functions.name: infra.docker.listServiceContainers
functions.description: Containers of a service the caller can read (only needs service.read). The result arrives in `infraOps`; read it with snapshots.opResult.

functions.name: infra.docker.reservation
functions.description: Memory/CPU reservations of the organization's applications on the host (reservation summary); compose services have no such fields.

functions.name: infra.docker.run
functions.description: Containers, images, volumes, networks and swarm nodes. Mutating actions refresh the matching snapshot when they finish; inspect-style actions put their result in `infraOps` (read it with snapshots.opResult).

functions.name: infra.docker.setDockerCleanup
functions.description: Turns the nightly clean-up of a server (or of the panel host, without `serverId`) on or off. Every night at 23:50 UTC it removes stopped containers, unused images, unused networks and build cache on that host, including ones Panara Cloud did not create. Volumes are never removed.

functions.name: infra.domains.expectedAddresses
functions.description: Every address the owner's domains may point at: the configured IP plus what a finished probeAddresses job of the same host reported.

functions.name: infra.domains.generateTestHost
functions.description: Free test domains: <app>-<hash>-<ip>.sslip.io resolves to <ip>.

functions.name: infra.domains.probeAddresses
functions.description: IP candidates: the server's interface addresses and its public IP, read on the host by an agent job (`{ addresses }` in api.infra.snapshots.opResult). Pass the job to validateHost.

functions.name: infra.domains.serverIp
functions.description: The address the owner's domains should point at: its server's IP, or the panel's configured IP. null means sslip.io hosts can't resolve.

functions.name: infra.domains.validateHost
functions.description: Validates a domain: does the host resolve to one of the server's addresses (or a known CDN)?

functions.name: infra.gpu.setup
functions.description: GPU setup: makes NVIDIA the default Docker runtime and publishes the GPUs as Swarm resources. It restarts Docker, so it shares the host's setup group and never overlaps a server setup or Traefik change. The status probe is the "gpu" snapshot (infra.snapshots.get / refresh).

functions.name: infra.mounts.readFileOnHost
functions.description: The file mount as deployed on the host, read by an agent job so the editor can show whether it drifted from the saved content. The result lands in `api.infra.snapshots.opResult` as `{ found, content? }`.

functions.name: infra.networks.importDocker
functions.description: Tracks existing Docker networks of the host.

functions.name: infra.networks.list
functions.description: Custom Docker networks that services can join besides panara-cloud-network.

functions.name: infra.networks.recreate
functions.description: Creates the Docker network again from the row (a no-op on the host when it already exists).

functions.name: infra.networks.resync
functions.description: Takes Docker's current settings for a row.

functions.name: infra.networks.toSync
functions.description: Networks to sync: Docker networks not tracked yet, tracked networks missing from Docker, and tracked networks Docker recreated.

functions.name: infra.panel.detectPublicIp
functions.description: Public IP lookup: the agent looks up the panel host's public address and stores it in webServerSettings.publicIp, which `webServer.get` returns. Any member's DNS instructions ask for it, so anyone may, but it runs on the panel host: for everyone but the instance administrator a recent result stands, and at most one lookup an hour reaches the host.

functions.name: infra.panel.lastUpdate
functions.description: The newest "Update panel" job: lets the Updates dialog show an update that is running, or the reason the last one failed, after a page reload too. The other panel actions (update checks above all) share the group, so each status is scanned a little way back for it. null for everyone but the instance administrator, and before the first update.

functions.name: infra.panel.runAction
functions.description: Reload, version check, self-update and the direct-port toggle of the panel itself. The agent runs them against the services named in its PANARA_CLOUD_IMAGES; results land in infraOps (snapshots.opResult).

functions.name: infra.serverSecurity.run
functions.description: Fail2ban, IP bans, SSH hardening, authorized keys and sessions on a remote server. Reads use snapshots (fail2ban, exposedPorts, pendingUpdates, sshSecurity, activity); each change refreshes the affected snapshot.

functions.name: infra.snapshots.get
functions.description: Live host state follows one pattern: the UI subscribes to `get` and calls `refresh`, which queues an `infra.inspect` job; the agent overwrites the snapshot row when it finishes. `pendingJobId` lets the UI show progress. A page that keeps refreshing opens a `hostSnapshot` live session instead, whose agent writes the same row without a job.

functions.name: infra.snapshots.opResult
functions.description: Result of a one-off job (inspect, Traefik file read, join tokens).

functions.name: infra.webServer.applyTraefik
functions.description: Recreates Traefik with the recommended version and the desired settings.

functions.name: infra.webServer.assignDomain
functions.description: Assigns the panel's domain: routes the panel through Traefik on the panel host and sets the Let's Encrypt account email.

functions.name: infra.webServer.get
functions.description: Every signed-in user reads the panel's addresses (DNS instructions need serverIp) and the panel-host flags their pages show. The rest (the administrator's Let's Encrypt email, cache cleanup, the template source) is the instance administrator's; users of other organizations share the instance and must not read it.

functions.name: infra.webServer.getLocalBuildsConcurrency
functions.description: Build slots of the panel host (the web server's buildsConcurrency).

functions.name: infra.webServer.setTraefikEnv
functions.description: Env vars usually carry DNS-challenge credentials, so they are encrypted and only decrypted for the agent applying them. `null` hands control back to whatever env the running container has.

functions.name: jobs.deployments
functions.description: Deploy history of any target (`deployments.target`) in the caller's organization, newest first, with the status of each run's job.

functions.name: jobs.logs
functions.description: Windowed so a live subscription only re-sends the tail, never the full log.

functions.name: live.accessLog.setCleanupSchedule
functions.description: Sets when the access log is truncated.

functions.name: live.accessLog.status
functions.description: Whether Traefik writes its JSON access log (the "Requests" view).

functions.name: live.accessLog.toggle
functions.description: Rewrites Traefik's static config and restarts it, so it shares the host's Traefik job group.

functions.name: live.monitoring.configure
functions.description: Saves the monitoring settings for a host. The bearer token is generated here (actions have an unseeded random source) and only used when the host has none yet or `rotateToken` is set.

functions.name: live.monitoring.setup
functions.description: Deploys (or redeploys) the monitoring service on the host.

functions.name: live.monitoringHistory.history
functions.description: The stored history of what a stats session would stream, oldest first. Authorized exactly like opening that session.

functions.name: live.sandboxes.templates
functions.description: The available sandbox templates.

functions.name: live.sessions.kill
functions.description: The owner of a session or an admin of its organization can end it; the agent watches killRequested and closes the stream.

functions.name: live.sessions.listOpen
functions.description: Open sessions of an organization: admins see everyone's, members their own.

functions.name: permissions.forMember
functions.description: For the permissions dialog: a member's current grants.

functions.name: permissions.projects
functions.description: Every project, environment and service of the organization, for the permissions dialog.

functions.name: platform.aiActions.deploy
functions.description: Turns an accepted suggestion into a raw compose service with its env, domains and config file mounts. It does not start a deployment.

functions.name: platform.aiActions.suggest
functions.description: Returns compose suggestions; creating the compose service from one is the compose domain's job.

functions.name: platform.deployTargets.remoteServersOnly
functions.description: Readable by every signed-in user: create dialogs and server pickers hide the panel host when it is set.

functions.name: platform.dns.get
functions.description: Takes the raw id from the URL: a malformed one is "not found", not an error.

functions.name: platform.notifications.test
functions.description: Sends a test message either through a saved notification or through an unsaved channel configuration (the "Test connection" buttons).

functions.name: platform.overview.backups
functions.description: Recent runs of the organization's database, volume and panel backups (overview of backups).

functions.name: platform.overview.deployStats
functions.description: Home "Deploys / 7d": application and compose deployments in the last 7 days and the 7 days before, counted over index ranges. `now` comes from the client (rounded) because queries can't read the clock reactively. Each count stops at the cap (`capped: true` means "at least").

functions.name: platform.overview.deployments
functions.description: Application and compose deployments of the organization, newest first (all deployments in one list), one page at a time; with the server each ran on and the application's build server.

functions.name: platform.overview.domains
functions.description: Domains of the organization's applications, compose projects and preview deployments.

functions.name: platform.overview.home
functions.description: The home page: service totals and status for the organization, plus its recent application/compose deployments (the latest jobs). Exact 7-day counts come from `deployStats`.

functions.name: platform.overview.queue
functions.description: Queued and running jobs of the organization (the deployment queue). Read by status so a long-waiting job is never pushed out by newer ones.

functions.name: platform.overview.services
functions.description: Every service of the organization.

functions.name: platform.overview.stats
functions.description: Counts are capped (`capped: true` means "at least"); Convex has no count operator and the home page doesn't need exact totals beyond the cap. Service counts (applications, compose, databases) and backup/domain overviews are contributed by those domains' own overview queries.

functions.name: platform.projectTransferNode.duplicate
functions.description: Copies the selected services of an environment (settings, secrets, mounts, routing) into an existing environment (the source one unless `targetEnvironmentId` is given) or into a new project. Built on the export/import sections with `includeLinks`, so the copies keep their server, registries, networks and git provider (the target is always in the source's organization).

functions.name: platform.projectTransferNode.exportProject
functions.description: Writes the project (and every registered section) to a JSON bundle in file storage. With a passphrase the payload is gzipped and AES-256-GCM encrypted with an scrypt key; without one it is plain JSON, so sections must not export plaintext secrets.

functions.name: platform.schedules.list
functions.description: Lists the schedules of one target: an application, a compose service, a server, or the panel host (targetId omitted).

functions.name: platform.schedules.previewNextRuns
functions.description: Previews the next run times so the UI can show what a cron expression and timezone mean before saving.

functions.name: platform.settings.get
functions.description: Organization-level settings outside auth. Instance-wide panel settings (server IP, Traefik, cleanup) belong to infra's webServerSettings.

functions.name: platform.settings.serverTime
functions.description: The clock shown in the dashboard header. Queries are cached, so the client ticks forward from this reading instead of re-querying.

functions.name: platform.tags.projectTagMap
functions.description: Project id -> tag ids for an organization's project list (and tag filter).

functions.name: platform.tags.setProjectTags
functions.description: Replaces a project's tags with exactly `tagIds`.

functions.name: platform.telemetry.remove
functions.description: Removing a provider drops it from every host selection and re-applies those hosts (an emptied selection removes the agent).

functions.name: platform.templates.baseUrlSettings
functions.description: The template base URL input of the "Create from template" dialog. The catalog is cached instance-wide, so the URL is an instance setting that only instance administrators change.

functions.name: platform.templates.list
functions.description: The catalog is instance-wide (hundreds of entries) and readable by any signed-in user.

functions.name: platform.templatesSync.preview
functions.description: Shows what a catalog or custom template would generate. Values are random on every call.

functions.name: projects.navigationTree
functions.description: The sidebar in one subscription: the projects the caller may open with their environments and services, and the servers, each cut down to what a row shows. `runtime` is what the status word needs beyond `status`.

functions.name: servers.create
functions.description: Adds a server. `enableDockerCleanup` is the nightly Docker clean-up; it also removes containers, images and networks Panara Cloud did not create, so it is off unless passed as true.

functions.name: servers.get
functions.description: Includes the attached key's public half so the setup screen can show the authorized_keys line.

functions.name: servers.getSetupScript
functions.description: The server's custom setup script; null means the default script runs.

functions.name: servers.list
functions.description: The organization's servers. Takes server.read: without it the list is empty, and `listNames` gives the names a member may see.

functions.name: servers.listNames
functions.description: Servers by name, for pickers and a service's own page: id, name, type and whether the server can take work (`state`), nothing else. With server.read or service.create it lists every server of the organization; otherwise the servers the caller's own services run or build on. The address is included only with server.read.

functions.name: servers.requestDefaultSetupScript
functions.description: The default setup script. The script is built by the agent, so this queues a job whose result (snapshots.opResult) is the script text.

functions.name: servers.resetHostKey
functions.description: After a server is reinstalled its SSH host key changes and the agent refuses to connect; this forgets the old key so the next connection records the new one.

functions.name: servers.services
functions.description: What still runs on (or builds on) a server, so it can be cleaned up before the server is removed.

functions.name: servers.setSetupScript
functions.description: An empty script goes back to the default.

functions.name: servers.setStatus
functions.description: Server status. An inactive server keeps its services (shown with a red server badge) but can't be updated, set up or cleaned until it is active again.

functions.name: serviceEvents.applyPending
functions.description: Starts the `primaryAction` of `pendingChanges`, worked out again here so a stale page can't pick a lighter one. It calls the same handlers as the deploy, rebuild and reload mutations, so permissions, checks and job creation stay theirs. Null when nothing is pending.

functions.name: serviceEvents.list
functions.description: Newest first.

functions.name: serviceEvents.listForOrganization
functions.description: Organization-wide feed. Members' pages leave out services they can't reach, so a page may hold fewer than `numItems` rows.

functions.name: serviceEvents.pendingChangeCounts
functions.description: Pending change counts for a list of services in one organization, aligned with `targets`; null where the service is gone or not visible.

functions.name: serviceEvents.pendingChanges
functions.description: "Changed since last deploy": config changes that take effect on the next deploy (see `appliesOnDeploy` and `reapplyOf` in lib/serviceEvents.ts) that no successful deploy, rebuild or reload has applied (or that a rollback undid), newest first. Each event carries the lightest `action` that applies it; `primaryAction` is the heaviest of those, the one action that ships every pending change (null when nothing is pending).

functions.name: sources.bitbucket.testConnection
functions.description: Unsaved form values override the stored ones (empty tokens keep the stored secrets), so changes can be tested before saving.

functions.name: sources.github.update
functions.description: Updates the display name and the app's page (https://<github>/apps/<slug>), from which install links are built.

functions.name: sources.providers.callbacks
functions.description: Where GitHub, GitLab and Gitea send the browser back to; shown in the connect dialogs before a provider exists.

functions.name: sources.providers.remove
functions.description: Admins can remove any provider; members only their own. Services that still reference it fail to clone with "Git provider not found".

functions.name: sources.providers.toggleShare
functions.description: Only the creator decides whether other members may use their provider.

functions.name: sources.registries.create
functions.description: Saves the registry and runs `docker login` on `serverId` (or the panel host), which both checks and persists the credentials there.

functions.name: sources.registries.listNames
functions.description: Names only, for members picking a registry for a service.

functions.name: sources.registries.remove
functions.description: Deletes the registry and logs the panel host out of it.

functions.name: sources.registries.test
functions.description: Checks credentials typed into the form before they are saved.

functions.name: sources.sshKeygen.generateKeyPair
functions.description: Returns a fresh keypair for the "Add SSH Key" form to fill in (and offer as a download); nothing is stored until the form is submitted through `sshKeys.create`.

functions.name: sources.sshKeygen.generateSshKey
functions.description: Generates a keypair and stores it like `sshKeys.create`; the private key never leaves the backend. Returns the public key to add to servers or Git hosts.

functions.name: sources.usable.list
functions.description: The providers a member may pick as a source on the service pages.

functions.name: sshKeys.listForApps
functions.description: Names for picking a key in a service's git source, open to every member.
